original_question: For the new asymptotically conical (AC) G2-manifolds constructed by Foscolo, Haskins, and Nordstrom that are cohomogeneity-1 under an SU(2) x SU(2) x U(1) action, which of the locally defined G2-instantons near the singular orbit extend to globally defined G2-instantons on the whole manifold X, and, once the global solutions are classified and a nontrivial family is found, what global properties does the resulting moduli space have? In particular, what happens for the D7 family from [FHN18]?
target_in_paper: Section 3.3(a), Open problems: for the new AC G2-manifolds X of [FHN18], determine how many local SU(2) x SU(2) x U(1)-symmetric G2-instantons near the singular orbit extend globally on X, and then study the global moduli-space properties of any resulting nontrivial family, especially for the D7 family. ([discovery.ucl.ac.uk](https://discovery.ucl.ac.uk/10067480/1/1812.11867v1.pdf))
correct_elements: The draft already matches the paper very closely: it identifies the [FHN18] AC G2-manifolds, the cohomogeneity-1 SU(2) x SU(2) x U(1) symmetry, the local-versus-global extension problem for G2-instantons near the singular orbit, the follow-up moduli-space question after one finds a nontrivial global family, and the special emphasis on the D7 family. ([discovery.ucl.ac.uk](https://discovery.ucl.ac.uk/10067480/1/1812.11867v1.pdf))
missing_details: The paper formulates this as an open problem in Section 3.3(a), not as a theorem or conjecture. ([discovery.ucl.ac.uk](https://discovery.ucl.ac.uk/10067480/1/1812.11867v1.pdf))

To be fully stand-alone, X should be introduced explicitly as one of the infinitely many asymptotically conical G2-manifolds constructed in [FHN18]. ([discovery.ucl.ac.uk](https://discovery.ucl.ac.uk/10067480/1/1812.11867v1.pdf))

The scope is the symmetry class to which the [LO18] cohomogeneity-1 theory applies, namely SU(2) x SU(2) x U(1)-invariant G2-instantons; the paper does not broaden this to arbitrary non-invariant instantons. ([discovery.ucl.ac.uk](https://discovery.ucl.ac.uk/10067480/1/1812.11867v1.pdf))

The paper takes local existence near the singular orbit as already guaranteed by that symmetry theory; the unresolved part is to determine how many of those local solutions extend globally on X. ([discovery.ucl.ac.uk](https://discovery.ucl.ac.uk/10067480/1/1812.11867v1.pdf))

To make "global properties of the moduli space" stand-alone, it helps to anchor the phrase to the Bryant-Salamon discussion immediately above: a noncompact moduli space, possible compactification by adding a limit instanton, and limiting phenomena such as bubbling/removable-singularity behavior. ([discovery.ucl.ac.uk](https://discovery.ucl.ac.uk/10067480/1/1812.11867v1.pdf))

The paper singles out the D7 family specifically because it was not considered in [LO18]; including that motivation makes the question more paper-faithful. ([discovery.ucl.ac.uk](https://discovery.ucl.ac.uk/10067480/1/1812.11867v1.pdf))
refined_question: Let X be one of the infinitely many asymptotically conical G2-manifolds constructed in [FHN18], each cohomogeneity-1 under SU(2) x SU(2) x U(1). For the SU(2) x SU(2) x U(1)-invariant G2-instantons whose local existence near the singular orbit of X is guaranteed by the cohomogeneity-1 theory reviewed in [LO18], how many of these local solutions extend to globally defined G2-instantons on all of X? After classifying the global solutions, and assuming a nontrivial family exists, what global features does the resulting moduli space exhibit—especially the kinds of phenomena seen in the Bryant-Salamon case, such as noncompactness/compactification and limiting or bubbling behavior—and in particular what happens for the D7 family of [FHN18], which was not considered in [LO18]? ([discovery.ucl.ac.uk](https://discovery.ucl.ac.uk/10067480/1/1812.11867v1.pdf))
justification: The draft clearly targets the AC open problem in Section 3.3(a): the survey states that the new [FHN18] AC G2-manifolds X are cohomogeneity-1 under SU(2) x SU(2) x U(1), that the symmetry-based theory from [LO18] guarantees local G2-instantons near the singular orbit, and that the open question is how many of those local solutions extend globally on X; once such global solutions are classified and a nontrivial family is found, one should study global properties of the moduli space, with special interest in the D7 family. The natural interpretation of "global properties" comes from the immediately preceding Bryant-Salamon discussion in Section 3.2.4, where the authors analyze a noncompact 1-parameter moduli space, its compactification, and limiting phenomena including bubbling, a removable-singularity limit, and conservation of energy. ([discovery.ucl.ac.uk](https://discovery.ucl.ac.uk/10067480/1/1812.11867v1.pdf))
